patient_information: A 36-year-old male restaurant owner from Europe, married.
chief_complaint: A mobile itchy mass under his skin, currently on his right shoulder.
history_of_present_illness: Three weeks ago, he noted a mass in his groin for 4 days, which then subsided. An itchy, serpiginous rash subsequently tracked from his groin to his chest, moving over several days and disappearing, before the mass reappeared on his right shoulder. There was no history of fever or systemic illness.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Five weeks prior, he returned from a fishing holiday with four friends to the Okavango Delta in Botswana, where he swam in fresh river water and ate freshwater fish from the river, specifically mentioning making sushi from fresh fish caught in the river. Two of his four friends had similar complaints.
physical_exam: Organ system examination was normal. On his right upper deltoid, there was a firm mass with clear margins, 3 x 8 cm in size, which had recently migrated across his upper chest wall, and a serpiginous tract was visible. There was no additional rash or lymphadenopathy.
labs_and_diagnostics: Total white cell count 8.9 ×10^9/L, eosinophil count 0.9 × 10^9/L, normal liver function tests, creatinine and electrolytes. HIV antibodies were negative. Serology for Gnathostoma was negative.
differential_diagnosis: Loa loa infection, sparganosis, larvae of animal hookworms or Strongyloides stercoralis, ectopic fascioliasis, migratory myiasis.
management_and_clinical_course: A clinical diagnosis of cutaneous gnathostomiasis was made, and the patient was started on albendazole 400 mg bid for 21 days and ivermectin 200 µg/kg stat. Over the next 6 days, the serpiginous lesion migrated over his shoulder and neck, disappeared for 24 hours, then reappeared between his eyebrows, moved to his forehead and face, and was felt inside his nose. On the sixth day of treatment, he expressed a larva from his nostril. Deaths from gnathostomiasis have occurred when the parasite entered the brain or spinal cord, causing severe neurological sequelae if untreated. His two friends received similar treatment with full resolution of their symptoms.
